title: What to look for
intro: Before the baseline, learn where each of the 7 universal expressions shows up on the face. Drag the slider from neutral to the full expression and watch the labelled regions.

cards.title: Happiness
cards.subtitle: Duchenne smile pattern

annotations.label: Brows: relaxed
annotations.detail: No brow action. Brows stay at rest.

annotations.label: Eyes narrow from below
annotations.detail: Lower lids pushed up, crow’s-feet at outer corners.

annotations.label: Cheeks lift
annotations.detail: Cheeks bulge up under the eyes.

annotations.label: Lip corners up & back
annotations.detail: Corners pulled obliquely toward the cheekbones.

annotations.label: Nose–lip fold deepens
annotations.detail: Side effect of the cheeks rising.

confusedWith.tip: AU12 only: the mouth smiles but cheeks and lower lids don’t lift. Check the eyes, not the mouth.
Contempt is one-sided (AU14). A smile is symmetric.

cards.cue: Look at the lower eyelids. If they rise with the lip corners, the smile includes cheek raising (AU6). This pattern alone cannot establish sincerity.

cards.title: Sadness
cards.subtitle: Oblique brows, corners down

annotations.label: Inner brows up & together
annotations.detail: Inner corners rise into a slanted “tent” shape.

annotations.label: Eyes heavy
annotations.detail: Upper lids droop a little and the gaze drops. Not widened.

annotations.label: Lip corners down
annotations.detail: Corners pulled down and slightly out.

annotations.label: Chin pushed up
annotations.detail: Chin boss wrinkles and the lower lip pouts.

confusedWith.tip: Fear also lifts the inner brows (AU1+4), but it adds AU2+5 (wide eyes) and stretched lips (AU20).
Watch the inner brow corners. That oblique slant is the most reliable sign of sadness.

cards.cue: Find the inner brow corners. If they slant up toward the middle, think sadness.

cards.title: Anger
cards.subtitle: Lowered brows, hard stare, pressed lips

annotations.label: Brows down & together
annotations.detail: Vertical lines appear between the brows.

annotations.label: Glaring upper lid
annotations.detail: Upper lid raised into a hard stare.

annotations.label: Lower lid tensed
annotations.detail: Lower lid straightens and tightens.

annotations.label: Nose smooth
annotations.detail: No nose wrinkle. That rules out disgust.

annotations.label: Lips pressed thin
annotations.detail: Lips tightened and pressed together, red margins narrow.

confusedWith.tip: Disgust also lowers the brows, but it wrinkles the nose and raises the upper lip (AU9/10).
Brow lowering alone (AU4) is ambiguous. Anger adds the glare (AU5+7) and pressed lips.

cards.cue: Brows down plus a glare plus thin lips. The nose stays smooth.

cards.title: Fear
cards.subtitle: Flat pinched brows, wide eyes, stretched lips

annotations.label: Brows up AND pinched
annotations.detail: Raised but drawn together into a flat, tense line.

annotations.label: Eyes wide
annotations.detail: Upper lids raised, white shows above the iris.

annotations.label: Lower lids tense
annotations.detail: Slight tension in the lower lid.

annotations.label: Lips stretched sideways
annotations.detail: Corners pulled horizontally toward the ears.

annotations.label: Jaw mostly closed
annotations.detail: Lips only slightly parted. No big jaw drop.

confusedWith.tip: Surprise brows are curved and not pinched, with no lower-lid tension and a loose dropped jaw (AU26).
Sadness shares AU1+4 but the eyes are heavy, not wide, and the corners go down.

cards.cue: Fear has tension everywhere: pinched brows and stretched lips. Surprise is open and relaxed.

cards.title: Surprise
cards.subtitle: High curved brows, wide eyes, dropped jaw

annotations.label: Brows high & curved
annotations.detail: Whole brow arches up, with long horizontal forehead lines.

annotations.label: No pinch
annotations.detail: Brows are not drawn together, unlike fear.

annotations.label: Eyes wide open
annotations.detail: Upper lids raised, lower lids relaxed.

annotations.label: Jaw drops loose
annotations.detail: Mouth falls open and the lips stay relaxed, not stretched.

confusedWith.tip: Fear adds the brow pinch (AU4) and horizontal lip stretch (AU20), with less jaw drop.
Surprise is the briefest emotion. If it lingers it is often posed or turning into another emotion.

cards.cue: Round and relaxed: arched brows, round eyes, open jaw. No tension in the lips.

cards.title: Disgust
cards.subtitle: Nose wrinkle, raised upper lip

annotations.label: Brows lowered
annotations.detail: Pulled down as part of the nose wrinkle.

annotations.label: Eyes narrowed
annotations.detail: Lower lids pushed up from below.

annotations.label: Nose wrinkled
annotations.detail: Skin bunches along the nose and the nostrils lift.

annotations.label: Upper lip raised
annotations.detail: Upper lip lifts and can show the upper teeth.

annotations.label: Lower lip down
annotations.detail: Lower lip and corners pulled down.

confusedWith.tip: Both lower the brows, but anger keeps the nose smooth and presses the lips together.
Contempt is one-sided at the lip corner. Disgust is symmetric and centred on the nose.

cards.cue: Look at the middle of the face: a wrinkled nose and a raised upper lip.

cards.title: Contempt
cards.subtitle: One-sided lip corner tightening

annotations.label: Brows neutral
annotations.detail: No brow action.

annotations.label: Eyes neutral
annotations.detail: No cheek raise and no eye crinkle.

annotations.label: ONE corner tightened & up
annotations.detail: A dimple forms at one lip corner only.

annotations.label: Other corner at rest
annotations.detail: This asymmetry is the whole tell.

confusedWith.tip: Smiles are symmetric (AU12 on both sides, often with AU6). Contempt is one-sided with no cheek raise.
Disgust is symmetric and wrinkles the nose. Contempt leaves the nose alone.

cards.cue: Compare the two lip corners. If only one moves, think contempt.
